stubs.service: Go module proxy / modernc.org SQLite driver (build-time only)
stubs.how: proxy.golang.org and dl.google.com are unreachable here. Go 1.27.4 comes from GitHub's actions/go-versions mirror via mise's http backend. Modules come from their GitHub mirrors via gomods/fetch.py and a go.work with local replaces; backend/go.mod is unchanged. modernc.org/libc has no GitHub mirror, so gomods/shims/sqlite registers the 'sqlite' driver on top of mattn/go-sqlite3 (cgo). That causes PocketBase's harmless 'modernc.org/libc version' startup warning. The binary is also built with `go build -overlay gomods/overlay.json`, which replaces Go's net/sendfile_nonwindows.go so sendfile(2) counts as unsupported. The sandbox rejects that syscall, and without the overlay net/http cut every static file off after its first 512 bytes (ERR_CONTENT_LENGTH_MISMATCH).

notes: ENTRY is /login, the app's sign-in page. Opening / without a session makes SecureRoute call POST /api/collections/users/auth-refresh, which correctly returns 401 for a logged-out visitor before the app redirects to /login. /login sits outside SecureRoute and makes no failing requests. Sign in with the login below to reach the trip list at /; auth-refresh then returns 200. Surmai is a PocketBase (Go) backend that serves the Vite/React production build. .ui-capture/build.sh rebuilds everything: mise install (node 26.13.1, go 1.27.4, pnpm 11.28.12; pnpm 12.18.0 from packageManager can't open its named store lock in this sandbox), pnpm install + vite build, the Go modules and backend binary at .ui-capture/bin/surmai-backend, and run/pb_public as a copy of dist/. start.sh runs migrations and serves UI + API on $PORT from .ui-capture/run (pb_data = SQLite, already seeded). Superuser dashboard at /_/ is admin@surmai.net / ChangeMe123. DATA: the app's bundled airports, airlines and places datasets were loaded through its own admin route (/api/surmai/settings/datasets). seed/seed.mjs then uses the REST API and the app's own save-transportation/save-lodging/save-activity routes (which create linked expenses) and the trip-import route.
